newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila to launch cocoa productivity project.
newsitem.headline: Manila to launch cocoa productivity project.

text.p: The Philippines plans to launch a programme to increase the country's cocoa harvests, the Bureau of Plant Industry's deputy director Benedicto Caballeros said on Tuesday.
Caballeros told reporters the Agriculture Department plans to develop 500 hectares of cocoa plantations in the southwestern Palawan island.
Under the plan, the government plans to extend credit, distribute better seeds and provide technical assitance to interested farmers, another Agriculture Department official said.
"The programme is part of the government's productivity programme on high-value crops," he said.
Philipine cocoa farms are mostly located in the southern Mindanao island.
Large commercial cocoa plantations have been broken down into small farms as a result of an Agrarian reform programme which required large land holdings to be distributed to small farmers.
Philippine production of cocoa beans has remained at a low level of 540 kg beans per hectare.
Domestic cocoa harvests have currently fallen to 7,000 tonnes annually, according to a briefing paper on the industry by the private group Philippine Cocoa Foundation.
Previous production figures were not available.

Philippine per capita consumption of cocoa has increased from 100 grams in 1980 to 260 grams in 1995. Domestic grinders require between 30,000 and 36,000 tonnes of cocoa beans yearly, the foundation said.
In 1995, the Philippines exported $20.85 million of cocoa and cocoa products, 74 percent of which is cocoa butter.
However, imports of cocoa products including chocolate confectionery and cocoa beans reached $47 million in the same year.
